name: Average daily rate
seoDesc: Average daily rate: work out number of rooms sold from the rooms revenue earned and the average daily rate. A free finance calculator with the formula,…
summary: Give the Average daily rate calculator the rooms revenue earned, the average daily rate, the average monthly revenue and number of rooms in the property and it returns number of rooms sold. Think of it as a shortcut for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Average daily rate calculator work?
sections.html:
The Average daily rate calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports number of rooms sold in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the rooms revenue earned, the average daily rate, the average monthly revenue and number of rooms in the property.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Average daily rate calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Number of rooms sold=rooms revenue earned ÷ average daily rate
Estimated average daily rate=(1 ÷ 30) × average monthly revenue ÷ number of rooms in the property

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Rooms revenue earned = 10 and Average daily rate = 10. Working through the relationship above gives Number of rooms sold = 1.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Number of rooms sold = 1 should be roughly the size you expected from Rooms revenue earned = 10 and Average daily rate = 10.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.
  • Shown in US Dollar, and convertible to any of the 113 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Average daily rate calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Comparing two offers that quote their costs in different ways
  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the rooms revenue earned, the average daily rate and the average monthly revenue — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Average daily rate calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns number of rooms sold, derived from the rooms revenue earned, the average daily rate and the average monthly revenue. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Average daily rate calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the rooms revenue earned, the average daily rate, the average monthly revenue and number of rooms in the property, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter rooms revenue earned in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Rooms revenue earned opens in US Dollar and the chip beside it offers 113 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Number of rooms sold = 1. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Average daily rate calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
